basis: Basal cell carcinoma originates in skin and infiltrates dermis; possible perineural extension does not establish common neurologic damage.
Congenital absence of limb skin with residual scarring; associated epidermolysis bullosa is a separate condition.
Umbrella for inborn glycolytic metabolic disorders; blood, muscle and nerve involvement varies by subtype.
Chronic suppurative infection of the middle ear with tympanic membrane perforation and epithelial ingrowth.
Rhodesian sleeping sickness; CNS invasion with meningoencephalitis is a characteristic progressive stage, affecting well over 30% over the untreated course.
Peroxisomal disorder; developmental impairment, seizures/spasticity, cataract and nephrocalcinosis with bladder dysfunction each reported in 1/1 patient.
Immune-mediated inflammatory bowel disease; intestinal inflammation defines the condition.
Destructive keratinizing epithelial lesion of the middle ear; preceding infections do not make the lesion itself an infection.
Optic nerve disease belongs to the ocular axis under the specified mapping.
Stable keratoconus remains a structural disorder of the cornea.
Congenital obstruction from atresia of the gastric pylorus; no evidence of additional intrinsic organ disease.
Inherited proline metabolism disorder; neurologic abnormalities are less common across the umbrella and do not meet the common-involvement threshold.
Congenital lower urinary tract obstruction directly affects the urinary system; pulmonary hypoplasia is not established as common across this umbrella.
COACH defines cerebellar disease, hepatic fibrosis and coloboma; renal abnormalities with elevated creatinine in 1/1 patient support renal involvement.
Lysosomal disease with skeletal dysplasia; developmental impairment in most and visual impairment in 80-99%; reported cardiac involvement omitted at the four-axis cap.
Congenital lower-limb joint contractures and arthrogryposis define the disorder; no neurologic lesion is established.
Vitamin D metabolic disorders commonly impair bone mineralization; rickets is the listed subtype and abnormal bone mineral density is an explicit feature.
Malignancy originates in the supraglottic larynx, which belongs to the pulmonary airway axis.
Lip carcinoma is classified here as oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma; the mouth belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Cataracts, intellectual disability and anal atresia define the syndrome; urinary tract defects, including rectovesical fistula and hypospadias, are defining features.
GH excess causes skeletal overgrowth/arthropathy and persistent skin thickening, each 80-99% in HPO; hypertension and diabetes are separately diagnosed conditions.
Autoimmune presynaptic neuromuscular junction dysfunction; weakness and autonomic symptoms reflect neurologic dysfunction. Associated lung cancer is separate.
Autoantibodies to insulin receptors cause severe insulin resistance; nephritis and cytopenias belong to associated autoimmunity. Acanthosis is a nondamaging skin marker.
A developmental learning disorder affecting written language; neurodevelopmental disorders belong to the neurologic axis.
Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism defines the disease; anosmia and Duane ocular motility anomaly each occur in 1/3 reported patients, meeting the approximate 30% threshold.
